clue.text: Strong wind from tandoor cooking

indicators.note: cooking is something being worked on and transformed, so the letters of the oven's name get stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A gust blows out of an Indian clay oven while the curry is on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' rearranges the seven letters of TANDOOR; the oven sits in the surface as the source of the blast.
explanation.definitionFit: A twister is a violent rotating column of air, the strongest kind of wind storm.

clue.text: Budget item is finished mind

parts.note: when a match is finished it is over
mind and head both mean the seat of thought

explanation.surface: An accountant says a spending line has been dealt with, so stop worrying.
explanation.definitionFit: Overheads are the running costs a business plans for in its budget, such as rent and lighting.

clue.text: Einstein's theory of where the over 80's go

indicators.note: a theory is a speculative rearrangement of ideas, here prompting the physicist's name to be reshuffled

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter, leaving the eight letters of the scientist's surname

explanation.surface: A whimsical idea that Einstein had a theory about where the elderly end up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theory' rearranges EINSTEIN. The definition is playful: people past eighty move on into their next decade of age, the one beginning at ninety.
explanation.definitionFit: Those over eighty eventually reach the decade from ninety to ninety-nine, the next age bracket up.

clue.text: Settles controversy to restrain explosive devices

parts.note: to deter someone is to hold them back or discourage them
mines are buried or floating bombs

explanation.surface: Negotiators resolve a dispute over curbing landmines and bombs.
explanation.definitionFit: To decide a disputed question is to settle it once and for all, ending the argument.

clue.text: Put on a northern river

explanation.surface: Someone dresses up a river in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wear is a river in north-east England that flows through Durham and Sunderland.
explanation.definitionFit: To don clothes is to have them on your body; the Wear is a river of County Durham in the north of England.

clue.text: A game shot in the artillery

explanation.surface: A sporting shot fired among the big guns.
explanation.walkthrough: In billiards, a shot where the cue ball strikes two other balls in succession has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: In billiards a stroke hitting two balls in turn has this name; it is also a heavy gun, collectively the big guns of an army.

clue.text: Barge into the girl

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Barge into the girl (7)': 'Barge' defines the answer, but no reading of 'into the girl' builds the remaining letters, and searches for the exact clue found nothing; probably cut short or garbled.

clue.text: Oceans fish by the shore

parts.note: oceans are seas in plain synonym terms
the ide is a European freshwater fish, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Ocean fish swimming close to the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: The ide (also called orfe) is a freshwater fish much used in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal resort or holiday is one on the coast, next to the beach and the waves.

clue.text: Indigene has turned middle aged, no?

indicators.note: has means holds within, so the native word contains the other piece

parts.note: an indigene is a native, someone born in a place

indicators.note: turned means the middle letters of the age word are flipped round
middle picks out the central pair from the word aged

explanation.surface: A local person asks whether they have now reached middle age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle aged' reads as a description of the native, but 'middle' and 'turned' work on the word aged, and 'has' is the container signal; the definition is the single closing word 'no?'.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusal or denial is a negative reply, the opposite of yes.

clue.text: Peas in Brazil, for example, are chicken feed

indicators.note: in means the Brazil piece sits inside the word peas

parts.note: a Brazil is a kind of nut

explanation.surface: Peas grown in Brazil are fed to the poultry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brazil' looks like the country, but it is the Brazil nut. 'chicken feed' is slang for a trifling sum of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny, trivial amount of money is slangily called both chicken feed and peanuts.

clue.text: Butter initially spreads to the limbs

indicators.note: initially means take only the opening letter of the word butter

parts.note: in American usage a spread is a large farm or ranch

explanation.surface: Someone spreading butter all the way to the edges, or over arms and legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreads' looks like a verb about butter but is a noun: American slang for ranches.
explanation.definitionFit: The limbs of a tree are its branches, the large boughs coming off the trunk.

clue.text: They create barrages of fish fryer's flour mix that is the point

parts.note: batter is the flour and liquid coating for fried fish
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, meaning that is
S, south, is one of the compass points

explanation.surface: A chip shop's batter recipe is the key to a barrage of orders.
explanation.walkthrough: Compass points N, E, S and W are standard single-letter pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Artillery units are batteries, and they lay down barrages of shellfire.

clue.text: A touch about turning paler

parts.note: a whit is a tiny amount, a touch

indicators.note: turning means the word for about is read backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone is turning slightly paler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning paler' looks like one phrase, but 'turning' reverses RE (about) to ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A comparative of a colour: more washed-out, closer to snow in tone.

clue.text: Dog on lead is a fool

parts.note: a mutt is a mongrel dog
to head something is to lead it

explanation.surface: A dog on a leash is being called an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' suggests a dog's leash, but it means to be at the front, to head.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull-witted person is insulted as a blockhead or dolt, the same thing.

clue.text: Toss archer from the bands

indicators.note: from tells us the answer is made out of these letters, rearranged

explanation.surface: Throw the bowman out of the musical groups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toss' looks like the anagram signal, but its letters are needed: TOSS and ARCHER are rearranged, signalled only by 'from'.
explanation.definitionFit: Large groups of musicians playing together are bands of a classical kind.

clue.text: Rabbit on about all night party

explanation.surface: Someone prattles on about the all-night party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit on' is British slang for talk at length; 'about' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk wildly or at length is to rabbit on; a large all-night dance event is the other sense.

clue.text: Words of convictions

explanation.surface: The words spoken in court when people are found guilty.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammatical units of words, and the punishments a judge passes after guilty verdicts.

clue.text: Missile thrown by skinhead at current dance

parts.note: the head of the word skin is its first letter S
current means present, now
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A skinhead throws a missile at a modern dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skinhead' looks like a youth but supplies the head (first letter) of SKIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Packed snow is thrown as a projectile in winter games.

clue.text: Matters about mid term rejoinders

indicators.note: about means the word for matters goes round the other piece

parts.note: something that matters counts

indicators.note: mid takes the middle two letters of the word term

explanation.surface: Issues surrounding the midterm elections and the responses to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mid term' reads as an election phrase, but 'mid' works on the word term, and 'about' wraps the synonym for matters around that middle pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Replies to an argument are retorts or comebacks.

clue.text: Home of the brave!

parts.note: the patriotic phrase from an anthem is reread with brave as a noun, a Native American warrior, whose dwelling is a cone-shaped tent

explanation.surface: A line from the American anthem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brave' as a noun is a Native American warrior; the clue reworks 'the home of the brave' from the US anthem.
explanation.definitionFit: Native American dwellings of bark or hide over poles housed warriors called braves.

clue.text: Seasons well at least twice

explanation.surface: Seasoning something well, at least two times over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well at least twice' means more than one well: a plural of a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: The first season of the year in plural, and water sources rising from the ground, more than one of them.

clue.text: Negative response for working at twelve

parts.note: no is the negative reply
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to work at midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve o'clock in the day is midday.

clue.text: Permissive development is quite majestic

indicators.note: a development is a change of form, so the letters of permissive are reorganised

explanation.surface: A liberal housing development is rather grand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development' looks like a housing estate, but it rearranges PERMISSIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something grand and striking is imposing, awe-inspiring.

clue.text: Suppose there is only half left of what Dickens made great

indicators.note: only the first half of the title word remains, the left-hand six letters

parts.note: Dickens wrote Great Expectations, so these were made great

explanation.surface: A reader wonders about half a Dickens novel left unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: Dickens's novel is 'Great Expectations'; 'only half left of' keeps the first six of its twelve letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppose something will happen is to anticipate or reckon on it.

clue.text: See ends of arm in needlework

indicators.note: ends of picks the first and last letters of the word see

parts.note: a wing of a building or an organisation is one of its arms

explanation.surface: Look at the ends of a sleeve in the stitching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends of arm' looks like one phrase, but 'ends of' belongs to 'See', and 'arm' is a wing.
explanation.definitionFit: Stitching with needle and thread is the craft of making or mending cloth.

clue.text: Cats with favourite dogs

indicators.note: with here means holding, so the whips word has the favourite inside it

parts.note: a cat, as in cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip
a favourite is a pet

explanation.surface: Cats living alongside the family's favourite dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cats' means the cat-o'-nine-tails, a whip, not felines; 'with' is the container signal, holding the favourite inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of slim racing hound related to the greyhound.

clue.text: He's first to say anything right on ruling class

definitions.text: He's first to say anything right on ruling class

indicators.note: first means take the opening letter of each of the following four words

explanation.surface: The head of the ruling class is the first to pronounce on what is right.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a Russian emperor, the man at the top of the ruling class whose word decides what is right.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian emperor stood at the top of the ruling class and his word was law.

clue.text: Made a fuss and over reacted

indicators.note: over means the letters of reacted are turned over into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone kicked up a fuss and overreacted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over reacted' looks like 'overreacted', but 'over' rearranges REACTED. In British slang to create is to make a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal British usage to create is to kick up a row or complain loudly.

clue.text: Employ fewer in vain

parts.note: to employ something is to use it
fewer means less

explanation.surface: Hiring fewer people proved pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: An effort that achieves nothing is futile or pointless.
